doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Kiyoshi Itoh's Tokyo albums
summary: She recalls albums recorded largely in Tokyo with substantial material.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What stands out for you in your memory – and I can give you songs if you need it – but I’m thinking about some of those lush albums that Kiyoshi produced with charts by Masahito Satoh. There are four or five, six albums in that batch that were almost harkening back to the early ’60s Capitol material. What stands out for you in those days and memories and times?

Right now, just that we did them. Don’t start me lying about how we did – well, a lot of them were done in Tokyo. That’s what stands out, that they were done in Tokyo, that Kiyoshi also liked the same kind of music that I liked. We did a couple of things in Los Angeles, but the bottom line was just to continue to do good material. That was my – that’s always been my – about recording – is recording material that’s substantial.
